ideas.pitch: A precision-engineered autonomous bot built to traverse randomized indoor obstacle courses using sensor fusion and computer vision.
ideas.title: Autonomous Obstacle-Crossing Rover for Arena Navigation
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the core judging criteria of IARC (precision in design, fabrication, and intelligent sensor/coding usage) with a working physical build.

ideas.pitch: A compact autonomous robot utilizing embedded edge hardware to process live camera feeds for real-time path correction without cloud latency.
ideas.title: Edge AI Dynamic Pathfinding Bot
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the winning pattern of gnuinely hard engineering and a live-working hardware demo under strict time constraints.

ideas.pitch: A modular telemetry and sensor suite mountable on competitive bots to monitor structural stress, battery health, and wheel slip in real-time.
ideas.title: Precision Sensor-Fused Telemetry Rig
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the judges' focus on precision fabrication and intelligent sensor integration by providing quantifiable performance metrics during the run.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous chassis equipped with dual-axis LIDAR and wheel encoders to map unknown arena layouts instantly upon deployment.
ideas.title: Automated Line and Surface Mapping Bot
ideas.why_it_could_win: Showcases advanced spatial awareness and software-hardware synergy that consistently stands out in robotics-heavy competitions.

ideas.pitch: A custom 3D-printed mechanical actuator system with quick-release couplings designed for rapid task execution inside the arena.
ideas.title: Modular Quick-Swap Payload Mechanism
ideas.why_it_could_win: Wins on the physical design and fabrication precision metric by solving mechanical reliability issues that plague most hackathon bots.
